Recommendation: Once FIDO2 is enabled (see AUTH004), scope registration to an approved AAGUID allow-list via key restrictions rather than accepting any FIDO2 authenticator. Two documented caveats. First, CORRECTED 2026-09-09: earlier guidance here said AAGUID restrictions suppress the registration campaign nudge for affected users - Microsoft's own documentation now states the opposite for a specific case. Under the Microsoft managed registration campaign state, an 'AAGUID-restricted' profile IS eligible for the nudge, provided its allow-list contains at least one AAGUID for iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, Microsoft Authenticator passkey, or Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows (Exclude/Block lists are ignored for this check). An allow-list containing only other AAGUIDs is still not eligible. This is an active rollout (Message Center MC1469555, expected complete end of September 2026) - verify directly against the tenant. See RCAMP001 for the full corrected eligibility table. Second, Microsoft is explicit that key restrictions are only advisory unless attestation is also enforced: 'Use AAGUID lists as a policy guide rather than a strict security control when Enforce attestation is set to No.' An allow-list without PASS001 is a guardrail, not a control. Note also that removing a previously allowed AAGUID immediately stops existing registrations of that model from being usable for sign-in. Graph only returns the raw AAGUIDs on that list, not vendor/model names - see the 'FIDO2 Key Restrictions' section (Policy Inventory tab) for those AAGUIDs resolved to readable key names where recognized.
